items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...did you know Olatunji? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes. I respected the tablā players... [Interviewee then discusses Indian percussion and African drummers generally, but does not mention Olatunji specifically or describe a personal interaction with him.]

ctx.x: . . . interview, talking about the influence of Latin percussion and world percussion. We were talking about the Ecue project. That’s something we’re going to run right out and get. How about any other types of percussion? Indian percussion, like with Ali Raka, with Ravi Shankar or his son Zakir Hussein, or any other types? Or African percussion. You talked about the Latin percussion, with bata. How about – did you know Olatunji?

Yes. I respected the tablā players, the Indian – in fact Steve Smith is really into that now. Eddie Shaughnessy was into that for quite a long time, Indian music. Emil Richards went to India to study and also buy instruments for his work as a motion-picture percussionist. I respect that. I haven’t really gotten into it like I should, but I might want to listen to quite a bit of it, because I know, watching some of the tablā players and Ravi Shankar – I went to a couple of his concerts. The tablā player was…
